blocks.heading: 7-Day AI Builder Bootcamp
blocks.body: Day 1 – Scope: pick a costly real workflow; define user, task, baseline, non-goals, risks and measurable success. Day 2 – Ground: build retrieval with source metadata and a small relevance test set; inspect failure cases. Day 3 – Act: add one tool/API/MCP integration with explicit permissions, timeout, validation and fallback. Day 4 – Evaluate: create representative cases, rubrics/graders and regression thresholds for quality and safety. Day 5 – Operate: instrument traces, latency, token/cost and tool failures; add retries only where evidence supports them. Day 6 – Red Team: test injection, unsafe tool requests, data leakage, ambiguity and over-authority; tighten boundaries. Day 7 – Ship: stage rollout, human escalation, rollback/runbook, executive demo and measured adoption/task success.

practiceBody: Ship a production-style AI workflow with grounded context, at least one safe tool integration, an inspectable eval set, regression gates, traces, latency/cost metrics, explicit security/safety controls and a runbook. Defend when you would use prompt/context changes, RAG, fine-tuning, deterministic code or no AI at all.

items.title: 01 – Problem framing
items.body: Choose a real user workflow. Write assumptions, risks and research questions; avoid jumping to screens.

practiceBody: Problem backed by user evidence; research ethics/consent; coherent IA and task flows; accessible visual craft; component consistency; realistic states; interactive prototype; usability evidence; iteration from observed failures; documented tradeoffs; outcome metric or test plan; and a concise case study that shows judgment rather than decorative screens.

benchmark: Curated source set: Stanford GSB + Stanford Alumni + MIT OpenCourseWare + TED/TEDx + renowned communication experts -- Target: develop a repeatable executive communication system - not just confidence. Learners should be able to structure ideas rapidly, speak with authority and warmth, design speeches, tell persuasive stories, handle Q&A, listen well, and coach others using evidence-based frameworks.

items.title: BLUF / Answer-First
items.body: Lead with the decision, recommendation or conclusion. Follow with 2-3 reasons, evidence and the ask. Best for executives and time-constrained meetings.

items.title: What? -> So What? -> Now What?
items.body: State the idea or fact; explain relevance and implications; end with action or next step. Strong for updates, impromptu answers and recommendations.

items.title: Problem -> Solution -> Benefit
items.body: Define the pain or opportunity; propose the response; quantify why it matters. Strong for persuasion, proposals and product/business pitches.

items.title: PREP
items.body: Point -> Reason -> Example/Evidence -> Point. A fast structure for interviews, panels, debates and concise responses when you need logic plus an example.

items.title: Past -> Present -> Future
items.body: Establish context, explain the current state and point to the destination. Useful for transformations, change narratives and strategic updates.

items.title: SCQA + Pyramid Logic
items.body: Situation -> Complication -> Question -> Answer, then group supporting arguments beneath the answer. Use for executive narratives and complex recommendations.

items.title: Know -> Feel -> Do
items.body: Before writing, define what the audience should know, feel and do. Use this outcome contract to cut material that does not move the intended audience.

items.title: Story Arc
items.body: Context -> character/goal -> tension -> choice -> result -> insight. Keep a bank of signature stories that demonstrate judgment, values and lessons.

items.title: Duarte Sparkline
items.body: Move between What Is and What Could Be; widen the contrast, then finish with the new reality and call to action. Useful for transformational speeches.

items.title: Executive Q&A
items.body: Answer first -> rationale -> evidence/example -> bridge to the decision or next step. Acknowledge uncertainty directly; do not bury the answer.

items.title: Speech Architecture
items.body: Hook -> promise -> map -> 3 major ideas -> synthesis -> call to action. Use signposts, transitions and a deliberate close rather than a fading ending.

items.title: Rhetorical Control
items.body: Combine ethos, logos and pathos with contrast, tricolon, anaphora, antithesis, metaphor and purposeful repetition. Use devices to sharpen meaning, not decorate weak ideas.

items.title: What "Sounds Executive" in Practice
items.body: Clarity before cleverness. Bottom line early. Specific nouns and active verbs. Fewer hedges and filler words. Calm pace, intentional pauses and vocal variety. Warmth + competence. Strong claims are matched with evidence, uncertainty is named plainly, and jargon is used only when the audience needs it.

items.title: Executive Message Architecture
items.body: Take one complex topic and create 15-second, 60-second and 3-minute versions using BLUF, What/So What/Now What and SCQA/Pyramid logic. Proof: one-page executive brief + three recordings + framework-choice rationale.

items.title: Speech + Persuasion
items.body: Write and deliver a 7-minute persuasive speech. Use a strong opening, Duarte-style contrast, 3-point body, evidence, rhetorical devices and a specific call to action. Proof: script + rhetorical map + video + audience recall/action feedback.

items.title: Storytelling + Data
items.body: Build a five-story leadership bank: origin, failure, customer, change and values. Pair one story with data so emotion and evidence reinforce rather than compete. Proof: story bank + 3-minute story + data/story version + feedback.

items.title: Executive Presence + Voice
items.body: Practise posture, eye contact, gesture economy, stillness, pace, pause, pitch, projection and prosody. Remove filler, vague hedges and rushed endings without becoming robotic. Proof: before/after video + delivery scorecard + vocal/nonverbal self-audit.

items.title: Spontaneous Q&A + Coaching
items.body: Complete a hostile-Q&A simulation and five impromptu prompts. Then coach another speaker: diagnose structure, audience fit, presence and delivery; prescribe one measurable change. Proof: recorded Q&A + response map + peer coaching memo + before/after evidence.

items.title: Week 1
items.body: Framework fluency: rewrite and deliver one message daily using different structures; build 15/60/180-second versions.

items.title: Week 2
items.body: Speechcraft: deliver two structured talks; build story bank; deliberately practise rhetoric, visuals, voice and closing.

items.title: Week 3
items.body: Executive situations: run meeting update, recommendation, difficult Q&A, panel/interview and spontaneous-response drills.

items.title: Week 4
items.body: Expert transfer: coach two speakers, revise from feedback, then deliver a final 8-10 minute executive keynote + Q&A.

items.title: Day 30
items.body: Present portfolio: executive brief, speech, story bank, Q&A, before/after presence clips, coaching evidence and next 30-day plan.

practiceBody: Turn framework fluency into observable performance. Every exercise must produce a recording, written artifact, decision outcome, audience feedback or coaching evidence - not just course completion.
rubricHeading: Proof Rubric - Communication Expert Standard
rubric: Audience diagnosis; framework selection; answer-first clarity; concision; logical support; story + data integration; persuasive speech architecture; rhetorical control; vocal and nonverbal presence; listening; Q&A judgment; adaptability under pressure; ethical influence; ability to diagnose, coach and improve another communicator; measurable audience comprehension, recall or action.
